newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Solel Boneh valued at 470 mln shekels.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Solel Boneh valued at 470 mln shekels.

text.p: An initial public offering in Solel Boneh Building & Infrastructure Ltd values Israel's leading construction contractor at 470 million shekels, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The offering for 90,000 units of shares, convertible bonds and warrants for convertible bonds closed on Wednesday at the maximum price of 920 shekels, raising 83 million shekels.
The offering was oversubscribed by 45 times, with orders totalling 3.7 billion shekels.

Due to the huge demand, institutional investors will receive only a third of the 41 million shekels for which they had precommitted. Other investors will receive less than two percent of what they ordered.
Among foreign institutions Lehman Brothers had precommitted for 3.5 million shekels.
The shares will begin trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange next week at 47.27 shekels each.
A tender for 1.68 million warrants, each for one ordinary share, will be held separately on Thursday.
Solel Boneh expects to raise another 130 million shekels from the exercise of the warrants and conversion of the bonds -- 18 million shekels in six months and 112 million within two years.
The share component gives the public 9.9 percent of equity, but the figure rises to 42.1 percent when fully diluted. Housing & Construction Holding Co owns the remainder of the shares.
Solel Boneh had net profit of 60 million shekels in 1996 and more than 21 million in the first quarter of 1997.

In 1995-96 it had annual turnover of 1.85 billion shekels, against 1.45 billion a year in 1993-94. Its order backlog rose to 1.9 billion shekels at the end of April from 1.7 billion at the start of 1996.
Its parent Housing & Construction is 72.7 percent owned by its workers and 21.9 percent by Arison Investments, the Israeli investment arm of billionaire businessman Ted Arison.
Solel Boneh had cancelled plans for an offering in 1994 when share prices on the Tel Aviv market plunged.
The success of its IPO now comes amid a revival of the new issues market in Tel Aviv following a rally in stock prices that began at the end of last year.
